newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM again asks Peru for caution in siege.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM again asks Peru for caution in siege.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Tuesday repeated his concern at Peruvian police manoeuvres which have provoked gunfire from guerrillas holding 72 people hostage in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I'm worried if the terrorists have been irritated over moves of the (Peruvian) special forces. We are asking for care to be taken about such moves," Hashimoto told reporters.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas fired several shots on Monday at armoured vehicles of Peru's crack anti-terrorist squad who were parading around the residence and blaring military music through loudspeakers.
One of the vehicles was hit, but there were no immediate reports of any injuries.
On Monday, Hashimoto asked Peru to limit police manoeuvres around the diplomatic residence, fearing they could unsettle the hostages held by the MRTA.
